selected.rationale: Post-storage is the core persistence dependency in both the compose-post write path and the home-timeline read path. A delay here propagates unbounded latency and can exhaust compose-post threads if no timeout/retry exists.
unique-id must be obtained before any post processing can proceed, so a delay stalls every compose-post request. This exposes missing timeout and backpressure defenses on the earliest critical edge.

Losing post-storage immediately breaks post creation and feed retrieval, leaving no fallback or degraded mode. This confirms the system's lack of availability/recovery behavior for its central state store.

compose-post synchronously waits for home-timeline fan-out to followers; a delay creates unbounded latency and can cascade to thread pool saturation. It reveals missing timeout control on this write edge.

The user-timeline update is a mandatory synchronous step in post creation; a slow user-timeline service stalls the whole request. This exposes the same missing timeout/retry weakness in another critical fan-out.
Home-timeline is required both when composing posts and when reading feeds; its unavailability causes broad system failure. This exposes missing recovery/graceful-degradation behavior.
Dropping the home-timeline write can silently prevent followers from seeing new posts. This demonstrates missing retry or consistency checks in the compose-post orchestration.
Packet loss on the persistence call can result in lost or partially created posts. Without retries or rollback, the system cannot recover from this failure.
